analogy.boundary: A dated reading only tells you when it was correct; whether it is still correct today needs a fresh reading.

maps.analogy: a number describing ongoing electricity use
maps.doctrine: a statement about something that keeps changing

maps.analogy: the figure shown on the meter
the date the reading was recorded
maps.doctrine: the time the value was taken

maps.analogy: which meter the reading came from
maps.doctrine: the source the value was read from

maps.analogy: the procedure for taking a fresh reading
maps.doctrine: the rule for reading the value again

analogy.text: An electricity meter reading is useful on a bill only if it records the date, which meter it came from and how to take a fresh reading. The bare number says nothing about today's usage.

reader.counterexample: A page prints a running total once and leaves it up for weeks with no date and no way to recompute it, so an old reading looks like a live figure.
reader.does_not_prove: Flagging undated numbers does not make any dated number current or correct, and the rule for refreshing this axiom's own figures has not been written yet.

example.text: The fact-claim audit flags any changing number that carries no date or refresh rule with a fixed error code, so a live count cannot be published as current without saying when it was taken and how to recompute it.

reader.governs: When a value read from a changing system may still be stated as current.
reader.plain: A number about something that keeps changing is a reading taken at one moment. To be usable later it has to say when it was read, where it was read from and how to read it again.
reader.potential_misread: That attaching a date and source makes a number current, when they only make it possible to check.
reader.refuses: A count from a changing system stated with no date and no way to refresh it.
reader.requires: A value with the time it was taken, its source and a rule for reading it again, refreshed or withdrawn once the source has changed.
reader.why_it_matters: A number that was true once is not read weeks later as if it were still true, after the thing it measured has changed.
